cases.statement: One person: Sun 2023 Patient 2 (female, diagnosed at 20 months), carrying c.289delC (p.Gln97Serfs*17) and c.392-1G>C. The review 42885896 re-lists her as Table S1 #95.

people.label: Patient 2
people.zygosity_or_genotype: two GAMT variants listed (compound heterozygous presumed by the table; phase not reported for this patient)
people.key_phenotypes: severe global developmental delay, mild epilepsy, no speech, low blood creatine (39.45 μM, GAA 2.84 μM), extracerebral space enlargement with reduced brain creatine on MRS

| 2/F/20 m | Low protein diet, Cr [400], Orn [300–400], Cyclinex-2 and Pro-Phree^a | 2 y 2 m | Significant progress in movement and social interactions. Ability to speak 3–4 words. Mild epilepsy that could be controlled | Normal Cr and GAA levels | 70–80% of normal |

Patient 2 made progress in communication and simple conversations but was not able to speak long sentences after 3 years of treatment. This patient had occasional absent-mindedness and some abnormalities on electroencephalogram, which showed significant improvement with the use of anti-epileptic drugs (sodium valproate).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Developmental delay, epilepsy and absent speech with low blood creatine and markedly reduced brain creatine on MRS; the cohort was confirmed by MRS. Her listed GAA (2.84 μM) is inside the stated reference range (0.40-3.82 μM). Testing was by NGS; the gene content of the test and exclusion of other genes are not reported.

Genetic analysis was done by next-generation sequencing (NGS).
One patient with variants in GAMT gene and 2 patients with variants in SLC6A8 gene were excluded from CCDS, as brain Cr levels were normal by MRS.

segregation.statement: Not reported for this patient. Methods say parents' blood was sequenced for the cohort (cohort-level), but no per-patient segregation result is given.

quotes.quote: Genomic DNA was obtained from venous (whole) blood of the index patients and their parents and sequenced using an Illumina HiSeq 2500 sequencer (Illumina, San Diego, USA). All detected mutations were confirmed by Sanger sequencing

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.289delC (p.Gln97Serfs*17). Phase is not reported for this patient; the paper states only at cohort level that seven patients had compound heterozygous GAMT variants, and that parents were sampled.

Seven patients with suspected CCDS had compound heterozygous variants in the GAMT gene, suggesting the possibility of GATM deficiency.

Genomic DNA was obtained from venous (whole) blood of the index patients and their parents and sequenced using an Illumina HiSeq 2500 sequencer (Illumina, San Diego, USA). All detected mutations were confirmed by Sanger sequencing

functional.statement: No assay of this variant. The authors state, at cohort level, that MRS can confirm pathogenicity as a functional test; this patient had markedly reduced brain creatine.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing should be used to make a definitive diagnosis and MRS can confirm that a variant is pathogenic as a functional test.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice-acceptor change at intron position -1 before c.392 (from the HGVS; protein consequence p.?). The review 42885896 labels it 'Splicing'. No mechanism statement specific to this variant.

authors_classification.statement: 37305710 labels the variant 'known' without an ACMG classification. The review 42885896 states no variant classification; it says it excluded patients with VUS or likely benign variants (cohort-level inclusion rule).

During data extraction, duplicate cases were consolidated, and patients harboring variants of uncertain significance (VUS) or likely benign variants were excluded (e.g., PMID: 37228909).

concerns: Same person under two identities: 42885896 Table S1 #95 cites 'Sun 2023 Pt 2, PMID: 37305710'; GAMT-ID0361 is GAMT-ID0035.
42885896 Table S1 #95 also lists this patient as repeated in 'Sun 2020, PMID: 32820516' and 'Zhao 2025 Pt 6, PMID: 40105081'; those papers are not in this batch and were not read.
Her GAA (2.84 μM) lies inside the reference range given in the table header (0.40-3.82 μM) and carries no up-arrow, unlike the other GAMT rows; creatine is marked significantly reduced.
Phase of the two variants is not reported for this patient; compound heterozygosity is stated only at cohort level.
The authors call the variant 'known' but give no source in the table.
notes_for_panel: Only one affected person, described in a cohort table. Evidence for the variant itself is thin: no segregation, phase, functional or population data are given for it.
